verdict.summary: The current head adds useful revision evidence but does not satisfy the zero-diff reconciliation contract and leaves the new ancestry evidence unbounded.

blockingFindings.title: Zero-diff reconciliation still requires model review rounds
blockingFindings.details: For a trusted release-engine PR with an empty exact changed-path inventory, createPullRequestTarget still returns a normal review target and executeAutoreview unconditionally invokes runAutoreview. The new revision facts only inform those model rounds; they do not implement a trusted zero-diff admission or approval path. Consequently a valid reconciliation PR can still be blocked by unavailable model routes, contrary to issue #280's requirement that trusted zero-diff automation complete without model rounds. There is also no end-to-end test exercising an empty inventory through this path.

blockingFindings.title: Commit-parent evidence is not actually bounded
blockingFindings.details: FIRST_PARENT_PROOF_LIMIT bounds the number of visited commits, but parseExactCommitRecord accepts an unlimited number of parents and the code serializes every parent into a verified-fact string. A head-controlled octopus merge can therefore expand ancestry evidence up to the Git subprocess buffer and bypass the bounded target-context serialization, causing prompt-size or route failures. Bound parent count and total serialized evidence length and fail closed, with coverage for the limit.
